title: How cloud load balancers spread traffic across Cloud Connectors and take unhealthy ones out
aliases: cloud connector sessions failed during unhealthy

prose.text: Cloud Connectors sit behind the cloud provider's own load balancer, which decides per Cloud Connector whether it receives new traffic. {{native-lb-probes}}

prose.label: The probe.
prose.text: {{cchealth-path}} {{health-codes}} {{probe-checks-forwarding}} The reference Terraform modules probe the path `/?cchealth`: [[cloud-connector.aws.gwlb:health-check]], [[cloud-connector.azure.load-balancing:ilb-probe]]. The probe port range outside those modules, and whether it can change after deployment, is open {{gap:probe-port}}.
The console's Active or Inactive status is a different signal from this load-balancer health: [[cloud-connector.insights.connector-status:status-not-lb-health]].
What happens on the Zscaler side of each Cloud Connector, its tunnels to the Service Edges, is separate: [[cloud-connector.overview.gateway-failover]].

checks.do: Whether the load balancer marked the Cloud Connector unhealthy (a 503 or no answer on the health port) at the time sessions failed.
Whether the failed sessions were already established on that Cloud Connector, which can fail until the flow ages out, rather than new sessions.
Whether the deployment's health-check interval was changed from the template default (15 seconds Azure, 30 seconds AWS GWLB).
Whether each availability zone holds at least two Cloud Connectors and, on AWS, GWLB cross-zone load balancing is enabled.

native-lb-probes.statement: Zscaler integrates with each cloud provider's native load-balancing service; the load balancers send HTTP health probes on a port selected during deployment to determine the health of each Cloud Connector.

quotes: The Zscaler service integrates with the native load-balancing services offered by respective cloud providers.
The load balancers conduct HTTP health probes on a defined port selected during deployment to determine the health of each Cloud Connector.

cchealth-path.statement: Cloud Connector listens on the configured port for HTTP health probes on a path the help capture renders as `?cchealth`.

quotes: Cloud Connector listens to the configured port for HTTP health probes on the ?cchealth path from the load balancers.

health-codes.statement: A healthy Cloud Connector answers the probe with HTTP 200; an unhealthy one answers 503 or does not answer.

quotes: A healthy Cloud Connector has a 200 HTTP response code, and an unhealthy Cloud Connector has a 503 HTTP response code or no response.

probe-checks-forwarding.statement: The health probe is meant to show that the VM is functional and can forward workload traffic to the Internet & SaaS and Private Access Service Edges, not only that the VM is up.

quotes: Health probes ensure that the Cloud Connector VM is functional and can successfully forward workload traffic to Internet & SaaS (ZIA) Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges and Private Access (ZPA) Public Service Edges or Private Service Edges.

probe-intervals.statement: Zscaler deployment templates use a recommended default health-check interval: 15 seconds on the Azure Load Balancer and 30 seconds on the AWS Gateway Load Balancer. The defaults are meant to take unhealthy Cloud Connectors out of rotation efficiently.

quotes: Zscaler deployment templates use a recommended default configuration for health check intervals.
The Microsoft Azure Load Balancer defaults to 15 seconds, and Amazon Web Services (AWS) Gateway Load Balancer defaults to 30 seconds.
The default settings are optimized to take unhealthy Cloud Connectors out of the rotation efficiently

change-via-support.statement: The default deployment templates are configurable, but Zscaler says to contact Zscaler Support before changing any settings.

quotes: While the default deployment templates are configurable, contact Zscaler Support before changing any settings to ensure an optimal configuration is made.

all-active.statement: Cloud Connectors scale horizontally and are all active: adding Cloud Connectors to a group supports higher throughput per egress location.

quotes: Cloud Connectors scale horizontally and are all active, enabling organizations to add more Cloud Connectors into a group to support higher throughput per egress location.

unhealthy-sessions.statement: New sessions should go to healthy Cloud Connectors, but existing connections through a Cloud Connector that becomes unhealthy might temporarily fail until the flow ages or times out and the load balancer sends the session through a healthy one.

quotes: New sessions should be sent to healthy Cloud Connectors.

In some cases, such as existing connections flowing through a Cloud Connector that becomes unhealthy, the sessions might temporarily fail until the flow ages or times out and the load balancer begins to send the session through a healthy Cloud Connector.

az-recommendation.statement: Zscaler recommends at least two Cloud Connectors per availability zone, across at least two availability zones.

quotes: Zscaler recommends deploying at least two Cloud Connectors per availability zone and across at least two availability zones.

gwlb-cross-zone.statement: Zscaler also recommends enabling AWS Gateway Load Balancer cross-zone load balancing for all production deployments, so GWLB endpoints in several availability zones can use Cloud Connectors in all zones rather than only their own.

quotes: Zscaler also recommends enabling AWS Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) cross-zone load balancing for all production deployments.
This setting ensures that GWLB VPC endpoints deployed across multiple availability zones can use Cloud Connector in all availability zones instead of only its own.

probe-port.title: Health-probe port range outside the reference modules
probe-port.detail: The help says only that the port is selected during deployment. The legacy reference guessed the captured `?cchealth` was an extraction artifact for `/cchealth`; the AWS and Azure reference modules use the path `/?cchealth`, and the Azure module's probe port defaults to 50000 (80 or 1024-65535). Whether other deployment methods use other ports, and whether the port can change after deployment, is not stated. Part of ledger entry cloud-connector-08 (whose fail-open questions sit in cloud-connector.overview.gateway-failover:fail-open-egress).
probe-port.blocks: configuring a custom load balancer or firewall rule for the health probe
